Alright, the recent edits to src/commands.ts have been type‑checked and compiled without errors, and the new cost display logic and keybinding hints are in place. The next step is to verify that the runtime reflects these changes. I built the CLI with bun build and attempted to copy the freshly built binary from dist/glint into ~/.local/bin/glint so I can run the updated version.

The first copy attempt failed with “Text file busy”. That tells me the binary is still being held open by a running process – most likely the tmux session I launched earlier that is still executing the old binary. I tried a pkill on any process matching “local/bin/glint”, but the exit code 144 suggests the kill didn’t succeed (perhaps no matching process was found, or the process ignored the signal). I also inspected the binary after the kill attempt; it still existed with the same timestamp, and the tmux session was still listed. The error log from the previous run shows an internal React component failure, but that’s a separate issue – the immediate blocker is that I can’t overwrite the binary while it’s in use.

To resolve this, I need to ensure the tmux session is definitely terminated before attempting the copy. Killing the tmux session by name is the cleanest way to stop the child process that’s holding the binary. After that, a short pause will give the OS time to release the file handle. It would also be useful to double‑check that no other process is still using the binary; the fuser command can list any remaining users of the file, which will help confirm that the copy will succeed.

So the plan is:
1. Explicitly kill the tmux session named glint (and silence any errors).
2. Sleep briefly (1 second) to let the kernel release the file.
3. Run fuser on ~/.local/bin/glint to see if any process still has it open – this is diagnostic and won’t affect the flow.
4. Copy the freshly built binary from /home/lane/GR/glint-cli/dist/glint to ~/.local/bin/glint. If the copy succeeds, echo a confirmation (“COPIED”) so I know it worked.
5. Launch a new tmux session with the same geometry and working directory, running glint and redirecting stderr to a temp log.
6. Sleep a bit (1.0 s) to let the UI render, then capture the pane output (filtering out blank lines) and show the first few lines, which will let me verify that the new UI (including the cost display and updated keybindings) appears correctly.

All of these steps can be combined into a single Bash command for atomic execution, and I’ll include a description that clarifies the intent: “Kill session first, then install and relaunch”. This should finally let me see the updated CLI in action without the “Text file busy” obstacle.

Thus, the appropriate tool call is a Bash execution with exactly the command constructed as above.

arguments.command: tmux kill-session -t glint 2>/dev/null; sleep 1; fuser ~/.local/bin/glint 2>&1; cp /home/lane/GR/glint-cli/dist/glint ~/.local/bin/glint && echo COPIED && tmux new-session -d -s glint -x 110 -y 36 -c /tmp/glint-test 'glint 2>/tmp/glint-tui-err.log' && sleep 1.0 && tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\s*$' | head -14
